reader.requirement: Every I-O status in the 9x class that the implementation sets on a RELATIVE file must report an unsuccessful completion for an implementor-defined condition that none of the 00-49 values describes, with x defined (documented) by the implementor.
reader.edition-search: grep for '"9[0-9A-Z]"' and the two FileStatusCode constants across WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime and WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler: the only 9x values on file connectors are '90' (LINAGE, raised only by SequentialConnector, so never on a relative file) and '91' (KeyedConnector.RecordRulesFailure for relative/indexed WRITE and REWRITE); neither path, nor EcEmitter, IoStatusClass or DispatchEmitter, tests Edition, CobolVersion or DialectBehavior
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise '90' (LINAGE) and '91' (CODE-SET) on SEQUENTIAL files only; the relative file's only 9x value ('91' on WRITE/REWRITE of a character with no byte image) is not exercised by them

probes.printed: USE RL 91 / W1 91 [AB€D] / W2 00 / W3 00 / USE RL 91 / RW 91 / RD 00 [WXYZ] / RD1 00 [ABéD] / RD3 INVALID / RD3 23
probes.expected: a relative WRITE and REWRITE of a record holding U+20AC are unsuccessful with 9x (91), the USE procedure runs, INVALID KEY does not (91 is not an invalid key condition), nothing reaches the medium (record 1 then writes cleanly with a byte-image character, record 2 keeps WXYZ); 23 stays the standard's own value for a missing record

probes.printed: W1 91 [AB€D] / W2 00 / W3 00 / RW 91 / RD 00 [WXYZ] / RD1 00 [ABéD] / RD3 INVALID / RD3 23
probes.expected: without a USE procedure the FILE STATUS item reads 91 and execution continues; the same output at --std 2023 (rel9x_nouse23.cob)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.1.3.4 GRL2.6  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in GRL2.6

reader.notes: On a relative file the runtime's one 9x value is '91', a WRITE/REWRITE record character with no byte image in the file's character set, which none of the 1985 relative values 00-49 (§1985:VIII.1.3.4) describes; '90' is reachable only on a LINAGE sequential file. Both values and their meaning are documented in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-110.md. Probed at 1985 with and without a USE procedure; behaviour is identical at 2023.

refuter.evidence: grep of the runtime for 9x literals: FileStatus.cs LinageValueViolation '90' (SequentialConnector only) and CharacterWithoutByteImage '91' (KeyedConnector.RecordRulesFailure for relative/indexed); MessageStore 91-93 are communication status, not file I-O. '91' (record character with no byte image) duplicates none of the 1985 relative values 00-49 (30 is 'no further information'). Documented in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-110.md (exists). Probe rel9s.cob at --std 85 (runs/rel9s-001), the SEQUENTIAL access mode the reader did not try: 'USE RL 91 / W1 91 RK=00 / W2 00 RK=01 / W3 00 RK=02' (the failed WRITE consumes no record number); I-O READ then REWRITE with '€' -> 'USE RL 91 / RW 91', the next REWRITE -> 'USE RL 43 / RW2 43' (the last I-O statement was the failed REWRITE, not a successful READ: §1985:VIII.1.3.4 status 43 text), then 'R2 00 RK=02 BBBB' and 'R3 00 RK=01 AAAA' (nothing reached the medium). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.1.3.4 GRL2.6  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in GRL2.6'; 'OK  §1985:VIII.1.3.4 GRL2.5  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in GRL2.5'. The one reading: whether a character with no byte image is admissible 1985 source is implementor latitude (the computer's character set); the 9x rule itself holds.
